aspect_adaptations: memory_ownership is read as view-state discipline (what serializes into the 170 KB page state, transient marking, one-form design); concurrency is read as JavaScript Remoting/AJAX surfaces, bounded polling and multi-tab optimistic-concurrency expectations; toolchain assessment accounts for Visualforce being a supported but maintenance-mode surface with no retirement date announced.

assertions_contracts.best_practice: Matches the Visualforce Developer Guide's page-lifecycle model and the Secure Coding Guide's server-side enforcement posture.
assertions_contracts.evidence: No platform change alters page-contract or lifecycle semantics in the current release.
assertions_contracts.guide_position: Page contracts first: audience, inputs, record scope and API version declared per page; page parameters validated server-side in the controller before use; markup never assumes a getter succeeded (every failable value has a rendered fallback); postconditions stated per action; data-protecting precondition checks must run server-side, never only as rendered conditions.

bounded_work.best_practice: Every figure spot-checked against the current Salesforce Developer Limits and Allocations Quick Reference: view state 170 KB, response under 15 MB, 50,000 rows (1,000,000 read-only), remoting 4 MB / 15 MB / 30 s / 120 s, upload 10 MB, PDF 60 MB with 30 MB images, header 8,192 bytes - all match the guide's section 5 table.
bounded_work.evidence: The limits quick reference restates each of these values in its Visualforce Limits table.
bounded_work.guide_position: Written per-page view-state budget far under the 170 KB ceiling; at most 1,000 iterated items (page the data); 50,000 rows per request (1,000,000 read-only) treated as ceilings never plans; remoting bounded at 4 MB request / 15 MB response with 30 s default and 120 s maximum timeouts; StandardSetController capped at 10,000 records; PDF 60 MB / images 30 MB; header 8,192 bytes.

concurrency.best_practice: Consistent with the platform's documented remoting and AJAX behavior and its per-request (not per-user) transaction model.
concurrency.evidence: No current-release change to remoting limits or AJAX component behavior affects this section; the remoting figures verify under bounded_work.
concurrency.guide_position: Remoting calls configure buffer/escape/timeout explicitly with bounded payloads and a handled error path; actionPoller and script refresh name an interval, a maximum lifetime and a stop condition; concurrent requests (second tab, poller racing a save) are assumed to interleave, with record-version expectations delegated to the Apex guide's optimistic-concurrency handling and committed state re-rendered after conflict.

error_handling.best_practice: Matches the platform's page/action error model and the guide's own contract framing; nothing in current documentation prescribes a different shape.
error_handling.guide_position: Failed actions leave records unchanged (partial change is called a defect, not a style); invalid parameters render a defined error state rather than a half-built page; async failures report the true state ('not saved', with a safe retry) instead of a permanent spinner; unknown success is treated as failure until a re-read proves otherwise.

formatting.best_practice: Salesforce's Prettier documentation describes support for Aura and Lightning Web Components plus standard file formats (JSON, Markdown, HTML, JavaScript), with Apex available via the prettier-plugin-apex plugin; it does not name Visualforce .page/.component files as a supported Prettier surface.
formatting.evidence: Whether the estate's Prettier setup actually formats .page/.component markup (via the HTML parser or a plugin) could not be confirmed from primary sources, so the guide's formatter claim is unverified rather than wrong - it needs an in-repo check of the diver/tooling configuration.
formatting.guide_position: Prettier, 'as provided by the Salesforce editor tooling', is named the one formatter with its version pinned per project, owning attribute wrapping, component-tree indentation and quote style.

memory_ownership.best_practice: Matches the Visualforce Developer Guide's view-state best practices and the documented read-only-mode ceilings (1,000,000 rows, 10,000 iterated items).
memory_ownership.evidence: Read-only ceilings verify in the same limits table as the standard ceilings.
memory_ownership.guide_position: View state is the memory model: one apex:form per page, non-transient state kept to ids/page numbers/step indexes, caches and recomputable result lists marked transient, iteration paged at UI scale, read-only mode adopted deliberately for legitimately large reads (raising row and iteration ceilings) rather than as a rendering license.

security.best_practice: This is the Salesforce Secure Coding Guide's Visualforce posture, including its canonical unescaped-parameter XSS examples, the four encoding functions and the no-DML-on-load CSRF treatment; the PMD VfUnescapeEl and VfCsrf rules encode the same two hazards.
security.evidence: One cross-guide caveat: controller-side CRUD/FLS is delegated to the Apex guide, whose security section is contradicted on the API 67.0 defaults (see the Apex record) - Visualforce controllers at API 67.0+ in fact default to user mode and with sharing, which strengthens, not weakens, this guide's posture.
security.guide_position: Context-correct encoding by sink (HTMLENCODE, JSENCODE, JSINHTMLENCODE, URLENCODE); apex: components' default escaping respected and raw-HTML merge fields treated as unescaped; escape='false' only for constants or sanitized rich text under a documented policy, each occurrence justified; no state change on GET (mutations only from user-triggered POST actions under the anti-CSRF token, Require-CSRF-on-GET when load-time action is unavoidable); sObject fields bound via apex:inputField for FLS; guest-reachable pages reviewed and tested as public attack surface.

static_analysis.best_practice: Code Analyzer v5's documented engine model confirms PMD is the engine that runs the Visualforce security category, and the two named rules exist in PMD's published Visualforce security ruleset.
static_analysis.evidence: The guide's architecture source (V3) and PMD ruleset source (V4) agree with the current Code Analyzer architecture documentation.
static_analysis.guide_position: Code Analyzer scan is part of 'done': the PMD engine's Visualforce security rules VfUnescapeEl and VfCsrf must report no findings on touched pages, with rule-selector names confirmed against the installed CLI (sf code-analyzer rules) because selectors are CLI-versioned surface.

testing.best_practice: Matches the Secure Coding Guide's threat model for pages and the platform's guest-user risk profile; adversarial fixtures are kept as reviewed data files.
testing.evidence: No current-release change reduces the guest or XSS surface this testing targets.
testing.guide_position: Half validation / half adversarial, org-side only: stored- and reflected-XSS payload sweeps per output context, CSRF probes (every state-changing path requested by bare GET must change nothing), guest-exposure checks executed as the site guest user, view-state abuse fixtures that must fail inside the page budget, and open-redirect probes on destination-like parameters.

toolchain_pins.best_practice: Current: Winter '27 / API 68.0 is the live line, Visualforce remains supported with no retirement announced, and Code Analyzer v5 is the current analyzer - the guide's pins and its maintenance-era scope are accurate.
toolchain_pins.evidence: The guide does not claim new Visualforce features for Winter '27, correctly: the release brings platform changes, not Visualforce markup features.
toolchain_pins.guide_position: SFDX project with per-page pinned API version (raising it is a tested change, since component behavior varies by version); sf CLI and Code Analyzer pinned; static resources versioned by name with recorded version/source/license, never CDN hot-links; LWC work explicitly routed to the TypeScript guide.

current_versions.code_analyzer: v5; its PMD engine runs the Visualforce security category (VfUnescapeEl, VfCsrf) the guide gates on
current_versions.prettier: Guide names Prettier via the Salesforce editor tooling as the markup formatter; Salesforce's Prettier documentation names Aura, LWC and standard formats plus Apex via plugin, and does not name Visualforce - see formatting
current_versions.salesforce_platform: Winter '27, API 68.0; Winter '27 brings no new Visualforce markup - pages take platform changes (including the API 67.0 controller security defaults), not features
current_versions.sf_cli: sf CLI v2, weekly train (2.153.6 at 2026-09-30), pinned per project as the guide requires
current_versions.visualforce: Supported, in maintenance mode, no retirement date announced; still the platform's PDF-rendering and Visualforce email-template surface

proposals.evidence: Salesforce's Prettier documentation does not list Visualforce among its supported formats, so the guide's current one-line attribution cannot be checked by a reader.
proposals.proposal: Verify in the diver configuration which parser/plugin actually formats .page and .component files, then amend section 23 to name that mechanism exactly (Prettier HTML parser association, or a named plugin) with its pin.
proposals.recommendation: Verify locally first; amend the guide text to whatever the estate actually runs.

proposals.evidence: Visualforce is supported but in maintenance mode with no new markup features in Winter '27; the guide scopes itself to pages/components/email templates without stating the selection rule that keeps new work off a maintenance surface by default.
proposals.proposal: Add an explicit 'should this be Visualforce at all' gate to section 2: new Lightning UI defaults to LWC; Visualforce is chosen for PDF output, email templates, Classic surfaces and existing pages - stated as the guide's own scope rule.
proposals.recommendation: Adopt as a scope note - it changes no existing rule, only the entry decision.
